answer.evidence: This is an east-facing chair drawn as a flat side profile, like the red 'side elevation chair' reference. The seat is a thin horizontal strip at rows 25-27, 12 px wide, with a dark outline at row 24 and a dark gap at row 28 under it. Its lightness falls from #ddbf91 to #cba76c to #a67a37, which reads as a lit edge shading into a thin side face, not as a foreshortened seat plane. There is no ellipse, no front-edge line with eave shadow, and no depth. The backrest at x=3-6 is a vertical post (exempt as seat_back) and the legs at rows 28-31 are thin vertical supports. The sitting surface shows no top, only a 2-3 row strip, so it reads as front_elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny chair of about 10x14 px drawn with only 6 distinct colours in total. It reads as a flat silhouette of one or two wood tones with a darker line, about 2-3 shading steps. The bench reference has about 14 colours and shows several wood steps with grain and a highlight edge, and the other references (well, stall, hedge) carry 9-20 visible tones per tile. The candidate has no visible grain, no highlight on the seat or back and no per-slat shading. The 0 tone count only means the piece is smaller than one tile, so I judged by eye. The 0% neutral edge share suggests tinted outlines, but with so few colours the outline is just the darkest wood tone on a flat shape, so it is not a selective material-tone outline. Next to the bench it looks thinner, flatter and more sticker-like, so it fails.
